pages.text: $(bold)The Fuel Cell$(0) is the reactor's "lunchbox": liquid fuel must be canned in metal before it can be stuffed into a fuel slot.$(li)Capacity: $(bold)10 L = 10,000 mb$(0)$(li)Filled by the $(bold)Fuel Canner$(0); an empty cell can be reused over and over$(li)What's inside decides everything — the same can performs very differently (see page 3)$(br2)For the full liquid-to-can line, see "$(l:akaishi:liquid_fuel)Liquid Fuel Chain$(/l)".

$(bold)Heat Sinks$(0) are the reactor's main cooling muscle — six grades: $(bold)Poor → Normal → Good → Fine → Exquisite → Ultimate$(0), crafted up tier by tier.$(li)Heat removal climbs from about 1% to 7%; higher grades cool harder and last longer$(li)Fit them into the reactor's cooling components, and they only work $(4)touching a fuel rod$(0)$(li)$(4)Consumables$(0): they wear down while the reactor runs — swap in fresh ones when they break$(br2)Starter recipe: 1 Cooling Base + 4 Copper Ingots = 1 Poor Heat Sink.

$(bold)Picking fuel = picking profit:$(0) the liquid inside sets the energy utilization multiplier — World Base Fuel 3 / Nether Compound Fuel 4 / End Mixture Fuel 4 / Advanced Mixture Fuel 5 / Pure Fuel 8 / End Dragon Fuel 7 / $(4)Ultimate Mixture Fuel 14$(0).$(br2)Higher multiplier means far more power from the same can — the burn rate never changes, only the output soars. Choose fuel before lighting up: lesson one of the reactor.$(br2)Temperature is still the line between life and boom: $(4)400-700℃$(0) full output, $(e)850℃$(0) warning, $(c)1000℃$(0) explosion countdown — details in "$(l:akaishi:reactor)The Reactor$(/l)". Craving higher-tier fuel? Read on to the Liquid Fuel Chain and the Plasma Chain.
Suggested reading order: master how fuel and cooling cooperate in "The Reactor" → refine better fuel along the Liquid Fuel Chain → finally graduate to the Plasma Chain.
